Date: 2026-06-20 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Draft order form questions + invoice recipient

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending the draft order form last night. Legal flagged two items we need clarity on before procurement will sign:

- Minimum commit cadence: your schedule shows a single annual commit with two tranches. Can you confirm invoicing cadence (upfront vs quarterly invoicing)?
- Net payment terms: our default is net45. Your template lists Net30 and suggests early-payment credits; procurement wants to understand if Net45 is acceptable or if Redwood needs an amendment.
- Tax handling: will Redwood invoice net of withholding tax? We operate in multiple states and may need VAT/resale certificate handling.

Also — who should our AP team route the PO and final invoice to? (entity and email). We received a copy of an MSA redline, but procurement wants a short playbook for invoice routing and tax evidence to avoid delays.

Can you and your finance/legal partner send a one-page invoice cutover playbook and confirm the final invoice entity? We're aiming to have internal approvals by 6/24.

Appreciate it,
Emma
Sourcing Manager | Nebula Health
procurement@nebulahealth.com

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I'm looping in Kimberly (Finance) to confirm invoice entity and Ben (Sales Ops) for the billing cadence. I'll send a concise playbook end of day.

- Minimum commit cadence: The order form is structured as an annual commit, invoiced in two equal tranches (50% at kick and 50% at month 7) for cashflow predictability. If Nebula requires quarterly invoicing we can reframe to four equal invoices; that will slightly increase admin overhead but not affect total committed spend.
- Net terms: Standard Redwood template is Net30. We can accept Net45 for this account pending credit approval. If Net45 is required, finance will ask for a 30-day billing holdback for the first tranche until credit completes (typical for Net45 on new enterprise accounts).
- Tax handling: Redwood invoices US customers gross; any customer withholding needs to be communicated and supported with local tax forms. For Nebula, if you can provide resale/VAT-exemption certs we will zero-rate as appropriate.

Action items:
- Kimberly: please confirm the invoice entity and if Finance can provision Net45 with the described holdback.
- Ben: can Sales Ops draft a one-page "invoice cutover playbook" that covers PO routing, required tax evidence, attachment checklist, and escalation contacts? I can then share with Emma and procurement.

I'll attach the latest pricing schedule and a draft redline of the MSA for your legal team to triage.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan / Ben — quick finance take after checking the ERP and entity mappings.

- Invoice entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US EIN: XX-XXXXXXX). Send PO to billing@redwood.com and cc ap-team@redwood.com. We will accept PO references and attach the order form PDF to the invoice.
- Net terms: We can provision Net45 for Nebula Health after a standard credit review that usually clears within 3 business days. For the first tranche, Finance prefers to send the invoice with Net45 but mark it as "subject to credit" — if credit clears within 30 days we won't place a hold. If credit remains open past 30 days Finance reserves the right to apply a holdback clause. This is consistent with our recent enterprise onboarding.
- Invoicing cadence options: 2-tranche (50/50) — recommended to preserve pricing anchor; or 4-quarterly invoices — acceptable but will require minor billing schedule update in the order form appendix.
- Tax evidence: Please request Nebula's resale certificate and state tax exemptions up front. For cross-border VAT we require a copy of the VAT registration to zero-rate.

I drafted a short playbook (see below) — Ben please format and produce as a PDF for Jordan to share: 

Invoice cutover playbook (draft):
1) Purchase Order routing: procurement@nebulahealth.com -> billing@redwood.com (include PO number and entity).
2) Required attachments: signed order form PDF; PO; resale/VAT certificates (if applicable).
3) Invoicing cadence: default 2-tranche unless customer requests quarterly — note billing appendix change required for quarterly.
4) Net terms: Net45 subject to credit clearance — holdback may apply if credit not cleared in 30 days.
5) Tax handling: Redwood invoices gross; provide tax evidence to apply exemptions.
6) Escalation: ap-team@redwood.com -> kimberly.park@redwood.com -> legal.ops@redwood.com

Kimberly
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
